result_status: not a transcription gap but a known open problem of the field, and the source's Remark 6.5 is too optimistic in saying relaxations are available: Miermont (AIHP 2008), whose Theorem 2 is the conditioned statement the source cites, assumes small exponential moments and writes "by making occasional changes in the proofs below, one can show that a sixth moment for mu is sufficient, and we suspect that a second moment condition is enough" - so g''(1) < infinity is Miermont's own 2008 conjecture. It is still open: Addario-Berry, Beltran, Stufler and Thevenin, Scaling limits of multitype Bienayme trees, arXiv:2507.23241 (July 2025), prove the CRT limit for conditioned multitype trees under a FINITE EXPONENTIAL MOMENT condition. What is available meanwhile: a sixth moment by Miermont's own remark. The source's offspring law is special (a size-biased degree thinned multinomially, so the total offspring of a type-d vertex is Binomial(nu, s_d)), which may admit a direct route that the general multitype problem does not - recorded as a new open problem.

result_status: reduced, with the answer identified and one earlier claim retracted. The factor four is an artefact of the comparisons: one factor of two from using D* on both sides instead of D-> and D<-, one from the constant 1/2 in the two-sided criterion. The firework growth chain is asymptotically multiplicative with E[log U] = psi(c)+gamma, so the critical constant of the one-sided process is 1 (classical; here with an explicit drift and the subcritical exponent 1-c as the Cramer root of Gamma(k+c)Gamma(1-k)/Gamma(c)=1). For the TWO-SIDED process the criterion is max(c_R,c_L) > 1, not c_R+c_L > 2 as the first version of the memo proposed from a first-moment count of closed intervals: survival under max > 1 is a coupling (delete one side's reaches and the other side is exactly a one-sided firework), and (c_R,c_L)=(1.5,0.4) has sum 1.9 yet survives in simulation to size 1e9. Extinction under max < 1 is supported but open; the natural decoupling argument is FALSE, because a site at one end whose reach crosses the whole interval revives the other end at an order-one rate per excursion, which is also why the symmetric two-sided decay exponent is (1-c)^2 rather than 1-c (measured to within two per cent for 0.5<=c<=0.8, N up to 1e12). result_status: PROVED, with a limit: lbar_k e^{k/e} k^{3/(2e)} -> C_* in (0, inf) and l_k e^{k/e} k^{3/(2e)} -> (1 - e^{-1/e}) C_*. The recursion of the source's Theorem 2 is the law of the minimum M_k of generation k of the Poisson-weighted infinite tree (s_k(y) = P(M_k <= y), lbar_k = E e^{-M_k}); Addario-Berry-Ford (AAP 2013) Thms 1.1-1.2 give the median and uniform lower tails, Aidekon (AoP 2013) Thm 1.1 the convergence in law (boundary case V = e x - |u| checked), uniform integrability gives the limit. Conjecture 2, layer half, also proved: max layer = floor(diam/2) in every tree and L_n = e log n - (3/2) log log n + O_P(1) (ABF Cor 1.3 plus a Polya split at the edge {1,2}). The rank half of Conjecture 2 is not treated.

source_title: Essential spectrum for Brox-type diffusion processes (Yuichi Shiozawa, Jian Wang)
locator: (unlabeled, stated as "the key open question" in the Introduction); Section 1, Introduction
title: (unlabeled, stated as "the key open question" in the Introduction) of arXiv:2607.07410
statement: "the key open question: can random drift perturbations break the compactness of confining deterministic diffusion semigroups?"
context: The paper answers this affirmatively in specific regimes (Proposition 5.2) but leaves the boundary case δ>1/α genuinely open, stated in Remark 5.3 (see below).
result_status: ANSWERED (yes, the drift destroys compactness for polynomial confinement, also for delta > 1/alpha), in the form of the posted paper. Theorem 1.1: for delta > 1/alpha, lambda_ess(-L^{w1+V}) = 0 Q-a.s. if nu_+ or nu_- charges (-inf,0), and lambda_ess(-L^{w2+V}) = 0 Q-a.s. if nu_+ or nu_- charges (0,inf); no sign hypothesis. Corollary 1.2 (with SW Prop 5.2 for delta <= 1/alpha): if V_+(1) takes both signs and alpha < 1 or nu_+ charges both half-lines (e.g. V_+ symmetric), both semigroups are noncompact for every delta > 0. Open: alpha in [1,2), both Levy measures on one half-line, delta > 1/alpha - one operator is covered, the other is not decided. Proof: disjoint test functions (min-max), Levy-measure scaling, sup|V| <= x^{1/alpha+eps}, a jump <= -t0 c^{n/alpha} with quiet surroundings in infinitely many blocks [c^n, c^{n+1}] (scaling + Borel-Cantelli II), scale-profile test functions with Rayleigh quotient <= h^-2 e^{2 delta - m/2} + cutoff term. The 14 Sep row's 'for every delta > 0' without the sign hypothesis is narrowed to this statement: for delta <= 1/alpha only SW Prop 5.2 (sign hypothesis) applies.

source_title: Quantitative limit theorems for generalized Pólya urns with applications to random tree models (Morenikeji Neri, Pedro Pinto)
locator: Remark 3.7 (posed as an open question, not a numbered Conjecture); Section 3, "Main results: Quantitative limit theorems for generalized Pólya urns"
title: Remark 3.7 (posed as an open question, not a numbered Conjecture) of arXiv:2607.07309
statement: "If one can show that λ_max(symm(C_p J_p(R^⊤−λI)C_p^⊤))<0 for p=d or d−1 for all tenable, irreducible generalized Pólya urns, then not only would Theorem 1.1 follow, but one would also obtain quantitative rates..."
context: The authors flag this contractivity condition as unverified in general; establishing it for all tenable, irreducible urns would strengthen and generalize their quantitative convergence-rate results for outdegree statistics in random recursive tree models.
result_status: REFUTED (negative answer to Remark 3.7 as posed), in the form of the posted paper. Theorem 1.1: for two colours both readings hold for every irreducible urn, constant R01 + R10. Theorem 1.2: for every d >= 3 there is an irreducible d-colour urn with nonnegative integer entries for which both readings (p = d on mean-zero vectors, p = d - 1) fail under every ordering of the colours (balance 6 for d >= 4, balance 100 for d = 3), and a six-colour balance-6 urn with gamma < lambda/2 where both fail; read over all of R^d, p = d never holds (all-ones vector). Theorem 1.3: with gamma the largest real part of a non-principal eigenvalue, gamma < lambda and for every A < lambda - gamma a Lyapunov-built PSD P, positive definite on H, gives contractivity with constant A; no P does better than lambda - gamma. Corollary 1.4: NP Theorem 3.2 applies to every tenable irreducible urn with an adapted inner product, Theorem 3.3 exactly when gamma < lambda/2. Supersedes the 14 Sep row (five-colour p = d - 1 witness, one ordering).
